subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider/auth quota-bucket contract for Gemini project/account quota failures, and should the first implementation live in core auth/failover or a provider/plugin-owned seam?
rationale: The choice affects public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback semantics, status/probe output, docs, and upgrade defaults, so automation should not invent the product boundary.

options.title: Add Generic Quota Buckets
options.body: Introduce additive bucket metadata and cooldown semantics while preserving today's flat key rotation as the default.

options.title: Fold Into Pool Routing
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 own the bucket requirement before implementing this narrower Gemini slice.

options.title: Keep Outside Core
options.body: Require provider plugins or sidecars to handle project-aware suppression if maintainers decide current extension seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Add Generic Quota Buckets
recommendation.body: Introduce additive bucket metadata and cooldown semantics while preserving today's flat key rotation as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the generic key rotation feature and adjacent auth/provider config decisions.
